A 50-year-old man with a history of alcohol use disorder is admitted to the hospital with difficulty breathing.  Physical examination shows tense ascites, peripheral pitting edema, and scattered ecchymoses on the extremities.  Chest x-ray is normal.  Laboratory results are as follows:

Platelets120,000/mm3
Prothrombin time26 sec
Activated partial thromboplastin time30 sec

The patient undergoes paracentesis, and his breathing improves.  Intramuscular vitamin K is also administered.  Three days later, his laboratory results are unchanged.  Which of the following most likely explains the lack of improvement in this patient's laboratory results after vitamin K administration?​‌​‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​​​​‌​​​‌​​​‌​‌​​‌‌​‌​​‌​‌​‌‌‌​​​​‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌​​​​​​​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌​​‌‌​​​​‌​‌​​​​​‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌​​​‌‌‌​​​​​‌​​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​​‌​​​​​‌​​‌​‌‌​​​​‌​​‌‌​‌​‌​‌​‌​‌​​​​​​‌‌​​​‌​​‌​​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​​‌​‌​​‌​​​​​​​‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​​​​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌​‌​‌‌​​​‌​​​​‌​‌​‌​​​​​‌​‌​​​​​​​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​​
explanation:
This patient with alcohol use disorder has multiple findings of cirrhosis, including prolonged PT and thrombocytopenia, which can contribute to ecchymoses.  The liver synthesizes most clotting factors; progressive fibrosis in cirrhosis impairs hepatic synthetic function, resulting in acquired clotting factor deficiencies.

Factor VII, part of the extrinsic pathway, has the shortest half-life of the coagulation factors.  Therefore, its level declines rapidly when hepatic synthesis decreases, and PT often becomes prolonged before aPTT.  This patient's prolonged PT with a normal aPTT is most consistent with acquired factor VII deficiency; more extensive clotting factor deficiencies can prolong both PT and aPTT.

Factors II, VII, IX, and X undergo vitamin K–dependent carboxylation in the liver, which enables calcium binding and interaction with phospholipid surfaces during coagulation.  Vitamin K supplementation improves PT when deficiency of the vitamin impairs this process.  However, it cannot restore clotting factor production when hepatic synthetic function is impaired, explaining this patient's lack of improvement.

Hepatic dysfunction also impairs synthesis of other proteins, including albumin.  The resulting reduction in plasma oncotic pressure, together with portal hypertension and renal sodium and water retention, contributes to ascites and peripheral edema.  Tense ascites can restrict diaphragmatic movement and cause dyspnea, which can be improved with therapeutic paracentesis.

(Choice A)  Vitamin K deficiency can occur with severe malnutrition (eg, alcohol use disorder), fat malabsorption, or prolonged antibiotic use.  It impairs carboxylation of factors II, VII, IX, and X.  However, prolonged PT due to vitamin K deficiency should improve with adequate vitamin replacement.

(Choice C)  Factor VIII is synthesized primarily by endothelial cells and participates in the intrinsic pathway.  Its deficiency causes prolonged aPTT with a normal PT.  Hemophilia A is an X-linked recessive disorder caused by factor VIII deficiency.

(Choice D)  Thrombocytopenia in cirrhosis results primarily from decreased hepatic thrombopoietin synthesis and splenic sequestration due to portal hypertension; alcohol-related bone marrow suppression can contribute.  However, vitamin K supplementation would not correct this patient's thrombocytopenia.

(Choice E)  Von Willebrand factor supports platelet adhesion and stabilizes circulating factor VIII.  Its deficiency impairs platelet adhesion and can reduce factor VIII levels, causing a normal or prolonged aPTT with a normal PT.  Platelet count is usually normal.

Educational objective:Factor VII has the shortest half-life of the coagulation factors, so impaired hepatic synthesis can prolong PT before aPTT.  Failure of PT to improve after vitamin K administration supports impaired clotting factor synthesis (eg, due to liver dysfunction) rather than vitamin K deficiency.​‌​‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​​​​‌​​​‌​​​‌​‌​​‌‌​‌​​‌​‌​‌‌‌​​​​‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌​​​​​​​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌​​‌‌​​​​‌​‌​​​​​‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌​​​‌‌‌​​​​​‌​​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​​‌​​​​​‌​​‌​‌‌​​​​‌​​‌‌​‌​‌​‌​‌​‌​​​​​​‌‌​​​‌​​‌​​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​​‌​‌​​‌​​​​​​​‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​​​​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌​‌​‌‌​​​‌​​​​‌​‌​‌​​​​​‌​‌​​​​​​​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​​
